quest.title: Unfinished Story
quest.description: The story continues. For Ann, please keep going.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x15000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what is this place? Paimon's dizzy from that whole... getting sucked into the book... thing.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I remember this place. I know it. This is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It sure does feel like we've been transported to all sorts of strange places under weird circumstances after meeting Ann, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Sorry, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's fine. Paimon's not blaming you — she just thinks, uh, that Fontaine really is a magical place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, this is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo... Sounds like an organization the people from the Kingdom would set up in a different country!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The method of entry was pretty interesting too, huh! It was just like that picture book in the Annapausis... We read and read... and then we ended up somewhere else!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #I can probably come up with some nice things, and if I do, I will share them with you first, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Ah, an Oceanid. It's been a long time since I last saw one of your kind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! You're back, Caterpillar! How are things? Have you found anything?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The sunshine and the wind feel so good. Everything else seems normal.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So... there's basically nothing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, allow Paimon to introduce you two. This is our Oceanid friend, Ann. Ann, this is...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: My name is Caterpillar. A pleasure to meet you, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Likewise, Caterpillar... Huh. Have we met?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: My memory is fading, so that is quite possible. If I may be so blunt, what is your relationship with the Red Empress?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The Red Empress? I have no idea who that is, though the name kind of rings a bell.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then let me try another name... What is your relationship with Lyris?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: How do you know that name?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #I went through many adventures with Paimon and Knight {NICKNAME}, only to find that she was merely a character in a story.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, what's going on? Do you know Lyris, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Do I? Hmm. Ah. I think I know what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm also a victim of riddles, so I shan't play dumb — I'll tell you everything I know.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Lyris did indeed exist. She was an Oceanid as well, and Narzissenkreuz's name for her within the Ordo was the "Red Empress."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait? What? So what happened to her?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I don't know, though I do have a hunch.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Can you tell me?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I fear this hunch isn't worth bringing up. Besides, I suspect that you've already figured it out, being as smart as you are. Am I wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Figured what out?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The first thing you said to me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "My name is Caterpillar..."

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No, the next line!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: What my relation to the Red Empress — or Lyris the Oceanid, is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, you should visit Mary-Ann in the Annapausis, Caterpillar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe that will confirm your hunch.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: A reasonable suggestion.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #I won't be troubling you this time, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I'll go with Caterpillar.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: And me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, then... We'll see you back here later.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's fine. Just as "Mary-Ann" dreamed of a past tale, and the tale gave birth to me, I will also rest. In dreams, I might be able to recall more things.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Perhaps there might be lovely things there, too. If I do recall some, you'll be the first to know, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Got it. Alright then. Good night, Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Indeed. Good night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here we are, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I remember this place. I know it. This is indeed the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right? We found this place previously as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's just like what happened with the book in the Annapausis...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's right! We read and read... and poof, we showed up in a totally different spot!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That... makes this place something like a secret base, doesn't it? We don't even know where it really is, either...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you feeling more calm now, Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Yes, much better. Thank you, Knight {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...Or should I drop that title? It was all fake, after all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't say that, Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But...

choices.text: On the contrary, your story has only just begun.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s right, y'know. We've still got a whole bunch of adventures waiting up ahead for us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem. And... how shall one proceed in peace of mind without a reliable knight at hand, oh lovely maiden?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon! Paimon was just trying to encourage Ann...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Pfft...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: You're quite the knight yourself, Paimon. You're positive, and you've got a good heart. It makes me happy, truly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Oh, c'mon, why're you getting so serious all of a sudden...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #You're just less powerful than Knight {NICKNAME}, that's all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmph. Everyone's got things they're good at! {NICKNAME}'s got a good brain and sword-arm, and Paimon... Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And that goes to show just how strong she is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that aside, didn't you say before that the "Narzissenkreuz Ordo has deep links with the past," Ann? That's why we came in the first place.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes. However, my head's still a complete mess...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true... Hmm, Paimon knows! Let's put what we've discovered together real quick. When we were exploring the Annapausis...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh... Oh boy, Paimon's head's a mess too. Any ideas, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, and that's a real symbol of purity!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, that's Paimon — a gifted speaker indeed!

choices.text: You really are impressive, Paimon. See...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've cheered Ann up already.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes, you truly are impressive, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You two... And here Paimon thought that you'd try to tease her or something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're weird — yup, both of you! Hmph...

choices.text: On the contrary, our story has only just begun.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's discuss Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, Paimon's been thinking about that, too. "Mary-Ann" said that your birth was a "beautiful accident." What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I think it might simply be that my birth was a coincidence. Just as she said, I am someone she dreamed of — the form she took in the dream.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The things we experienced together were also part of the tale in the dream. If it hadn't been for you, that dream might never have ended...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Or perhaps it might have ended, and I might have disappeared with the "happily ever after." I can't be sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Not that Paimon gets it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This means that "Mary-Ann" is also an Oceanid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And Ann was created from "Mary-Ann."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That's what I believe as well. And if that's the case, the things I remembered during our journey should have been her memories... Or so I'd think.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your knowledge and experience cannot exceed that of the main body.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But when you met her, "you" also became your own entity.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Without a main body to restrict and control you.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So... "become the master of your own fate"... Her last words to me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, okay, Paimon gets it now. So, that means that Petit Chou, Al, and the others are creations just like you, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I believe that to be the case, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case, who was "Mary-Ann," really?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...This name is very familiar to me.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But I cannot recall why — it's like some part of my body has been frozen.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's discuss the Narzissenkreuz Ordo...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Alright. I now have a lot of thoughts on the matter — memories and emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: When those two children brought me here, it was a lovely place. Everything was new and shiny, just as before.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: They were vibrant and excited, like the sunlight shining on the water. They told me that this was our new home, and that they'd brought many new friends. That everything could be like they were before.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But later, they changed. Some things stopped being the same, and the people here changed, too.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Though the Narzissenkreuz Institute of old did not have sunlight, it was very warm. Yet, this place grew ever colder. And then... then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ann looks like she's in pain, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #I'm sorry, Knight {NICKNAME}... As for the rest, each time I try to recall it, I grow very frightened... and very sad. This is the best I can do for now.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I can sense that many terrible things happened here. I can sense many emotions — rage, terror, but also hope, trust, and admiration.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But all of them make me feel a strange sort of pain, like there are all sorts of shards or impurities embedded in my body. I don't want to... I can't...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright! Leave that aside first — there's no need to force it. The more you try to force yourself to remember, the less you'll be able to remember!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's discuss Princess Lyris...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I suspect that she was only ever a character in a story. In that tale, we needed to save her and defeat the fell dragon Narcissus.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That was my original purp{RUBY#[S]wish}ose.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All stories must have their origins.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Speaking of that, Ann, we've heard you mention a place called the Narzissenkreuz Institute before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So if we go with {NICKNAME}'s logic, the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom and Adventure Team might have their stories' origin in the Institute and the Ordo, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That is... possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Any other thoughts, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. It feels like we got our hands on some new clues, but then again not...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Actually, I've recalled something else.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I've seen terrifying sights. The primordial waters, the amniotic fluid of the world, and its placenta, devoured to the last. The world fell into utter darkness — never again would the cool spring water flow.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I saw that once. Or perhaps I saw that in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait a second. Which are you talking about? The past or the future?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I... don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Sorry, and thank you, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Come on, it's fine. We said we were gonna help you!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No. I truly am happy that the two of you are the first two friends I met since I became "me." For that, you have my thanks.

choices.text: Pleased to have met you too, Ann.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gah, why are the two of you being so... formal?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't becoming friends something that just, y'know, happens? When you called out to us and asked for our help, Ann, that was the moment Paimon thought — that's right, you're our friend, and we've gotta help you!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: *sniff* Thank you so much, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be like that, Ann. If you really wanna thank us, then keep your chin up, and keep those spirits high!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes... Yes! You're exactly right, Paimon.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Besides, I have your help — I shouldn't waste it by standing still. I must recall more, and tell you all about it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, not that you have to push yourself too hard to recall the past...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Ah, an Oceanid. It's been a long time since I last saw one of your kind.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, I detect the biological signature of an Oceanid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, allow Paimon to introduce you... This is our Oceanid friend, Ann. Ann, these two are Caterpillar and...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...I know — and Seymour, the silly dog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Relevant data does not exist. I do not believe we have had the honor of meeting, Oceanid Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I've never met you before, either. But I was sure of it the moment I saw you — you must be Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: This must be... No, I don't know, either. This is so strange...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's bring you up to speed...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share some information...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So, you're searching for Mary-Ann, Seymour...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh! No wonder that name felt familiar! The person Seymour mentioned and is looking for also goes by that name!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Ugh, Paimon's had it with you, you silly dog!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... Based on what you said before, they can't be the same Mary-Ann, right? The timing...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I deduce from your statement, then, that you have met someone named Mary-Ann in the past, or have perhaps read or heard about such a person from sources aside from myself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that was her name, that's for sure. Y'know what, let's do it like this — we can call the Mary-Ann in the Annapausis "Mary-Ann 1," and the one you're looking for, Seymour, can be "Mary-Ann 2"!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Negative. The Ms. Mary-Ann I am searching for is of a higher sequential priority. To prevent confusion, she should be "Mary-Ann 1" instead.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Huh? Why don't you look at it this way, Seymour. 2 is bigger than 1. Doesn't that make it pretty good, too?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Your claim... Sorting data fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, looks like he's stopped functioning again...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Hehe, silly dog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon didn't think you had any mean bones in you, Ann, but you sure do!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Haha. I don't know why, but I suddenly felt compelled to do that...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Preliminary data fragment sorting complete. For the following 15 reasons, Oceanid Ann, I assess that your perspective is illogical. Firstly—

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, that stuff doesn't matter. Come, good doggie, sit.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: ...Why?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: If you sit, we'll be able to improve photo-taking stability, right?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Yes. Do you need to take a photo, Oceanid Ann? I am equipped with the most advanced optics from the Fontaine Institute of Natural Philosophy. I can—

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Oh, there's no need, but thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's get serious now, shall we...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Seymour was completely being played by Ann! Anyway, you two have been acquainted now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yeah. Still, Caterpillar... have we ever met before?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: My memory is fading, so that is quite possible. If I may be so blunt, what is your relationship with the Red Empress?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The Red Empress? I have no idea who that is, though the name kind of rings a bell.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then let me try another name... What is your relationship with Lyris?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...How do you know that name?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #I went through many adventures with Paimon and Knight {NICKNAME}, only to find that she was merely a character in a story.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, what's going on? Do you know Lyris, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Do I? Hmm. Ah. I think I know what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm also a victim of riddles, so I shan't play dumb — I'll tell you everything I know.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Lyris did indeed exist. She was an Oceanid as well, and Narzissenkreuz's name for her within the Ordo was the "Red Empress."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait? What? So what happened to her?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I don't know, though I do have a hunch.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Can you tell me?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #It's just a small guess. But the story about the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom that you two mentioned, {NICKNAME} and Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let's just say that I think we can use it as a reference of sorts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... so no progress for us today, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, when we first got here, Paimon couldn't help but notice... The clock here doesn't seem very accurate, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Ah. That.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Simply put, it's the Doomsday Clock.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Doomsday Clock?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: When the clock strikes midnight, the apocalypse will come.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Doesn't this mean that the end of the world is almost upon us?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Huh, that really does take me back. When I was here before, they thought the apocalypse was still far away, and that though it wouldn't happen in our generation, we should stop it for the sake of the future.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If the clock is accurate, then it is not far off now. Perhaps we shall lay ourselves down to sleep tonight, and the sun shall not rise in the morn. Perhaps the sea shall evaporate tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Or perhaps we are already living in the apocalypse, and the good times have long ended.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Get serious! Will the apocalypse really come?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: What we're seeing is a doomsday clock, not doomsday itself. Time is just an invention by man to measure changes.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz was the one who used the "world-formula" to calculate the beginning of the end, and built this device.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: As such, I cannot answer your question, dear Paimon. Because this is all it is — a clock.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's share our findings...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon briefly share all that happened with the other three people (though technically speaking, none of them are humans).

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Input logged.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Elynas...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you remember anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. It's like water boiling off into gas. I can't see it, and I can't quite grasp it, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh. Any thoughts or leads, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Hmm... Can't say that I don't, but I'm still trying to sort some things out, so let's discuss this later.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Oh, I keep forgetting to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I'm very grateful for everything you've done for Lanoire. So, is there anything that I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Do you mean... anything? Just like making a wish?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Haha! It should be something within the scope of my abilities, of course. You did free Lanoire and I from prison, but I'm no Jinn in a bottle.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what would your wish be, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, if that's the case, then Mora... No, wait, yummy food...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Argh! Paimon wants lots of things, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been having lots of fun traveling together, so we don't really need anything special. Instead, Caterpillar, can you help us help Ann and Seymour?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Is that alright?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I understand. Then, let us work together.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Alright!

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: #Now, I plan to work with Seymour and Ann to see if we can use our experiences and the information available here to figure something new out. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's meet back here later.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #There is a chance that I might be able to think of some lovely things. If I do, you'll be the first to know, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, I detect an Oceanid's biological signature.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gah! You finally woke up!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Negative. My various previous clockwork cycles were spent collating fragmented data and searching for useful information.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, not that we're gonna be able to see any of the photos inside, will we?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, yes, let Paimon introduce you. This is Ann, an Oceanid and a friend of ours. Ann, this is...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...I know. You're the silly dog, Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I lack the relevant data. I do not believe we have had the honor of meeting, Oceanid Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I've never met you before, either. But I was sure of it the moment I saw you — you must be Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: This must be... No, I don't know, either. I feel... strange...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway, let us bring you up to speed...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You shed a little light on the matters so far...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So, Seymour is searching for Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh! No wonder that name felt familiar! The person Seymour mentioned and is looking for is also named Mary-Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Ugh, Paimon's had it with you, you silly dog!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... According to what Seymour said before, they can't be the same Mary-Ann, right? The timing...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Based on your statement, may I deduce that you have met someone named Mary-Ann in the past, or perhaps read or heard about such a person from sources apart from myself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that was her name, that's for sure. Y'know what, let's do it like this — we can call the Mary-Ann in the Annapausis "Mary-Ann 1," and the one you're looking for, Seymour, can be "Mary-Ann 2"!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Negative. The Ms. Mary-Ann I am searching for is of a higher sequential priority. To prevent confusion, she should be "Mary-Ann 1" instead.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Huh? Why don't you look at it this way, Seymour. 2 is bigger than 1. Doesn't that make it pretty good, too?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Your claim... Sorting data fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, looks like he's stopped functioning again...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Hehe, silly dog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon didn't think you had any mean bones in you, Ann, but you sure do!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Haha. I don't know why, but I suddenly felt compelled to do that...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Preliminary data fragment sorting complete. For the following 15 reasons, Oceanid Ann, I assess that your perspective is illogical. Firstly—

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, that stuff doesn't matter. Come, good doggie, sit.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: ...Why?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: If you sit, we'll be able to improve photo-taking stability, right?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Yes. Do you need to take a photo, Oceanid Ann? I am equipped with the most advanced optics from the Fontaine Institute of Natural Philosophy. I can—

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Oh, there's no need, but thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Seymour's getting played left and right over here!

choices.text: Let's call a quick halt, please...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really... Anyway, wanna go to the Annapausis, Seymour? That way, you can meet that "Mary-Ann" and see if she's the one you're looking for or not.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: What you say makes sense, Paimon.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Affirmative. A reasonable suggestion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, then let's go!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Actually, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon, I don't think we'll need to trouble you this time. I can show Seymour the way!

choices.text: Are you sure you'll be fine?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes. I know Seymour's very reliable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! We'll meet back here later, alright?

choices.text: Do you want to go to the Annapausis, Seymour?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. That way, you can meet that "Mary-Ann" and see if she's the one you're looking for or not!
